trigger: A principal holds two roles: role A had a seeded default permission revoked (tombstoned effect='deny'); role C independently grants the SAME permission
summary: The post-G4-HP-01 deny-tombstone fix diverges from legacy semantics for dual-role principals: legacy computed ALLOW (absence of a row is neutral, a different role's grant controls); the tombstone computes DENY, because check_permission()/check_scoped_permission()/authorize_list_read() all apply 'deny overrides everything across ALL of a principal's held roles'. Verified on both the global check and the management-group-scoped confinement path (role_effects_for -> resolve_perm_groups's deny_groups -> expand_visible_set subtracting whole agent subtrees).
classification_rationale: Reasoned from code actually read across all three authorization-decision call sites; empirically confirmed via a temporary probe test before the redesign.

trigger: grant()'s WHERE NOT EXISTS(marker) INSERT blocks on the ON CONFLICT arbiter waiting for a concurrent remove_permission()/backfill transaction's uncommitted DELETE
summary: CHAOS-1: grant()'s READ COMMITTED snapshot is fixed at statement start; once it blocks on the arbiter and the concurrent revoke commits, Postgres re-checks only the (now-gone) conflict target and never re-evaluates WHERE NOT EXISTS — the revoked permission resurrects permanently, both the row and the marker end up present, with no self-correction. Reproducible via a live two-connection libpq test (3/3). Live today via migrate_from_sqlite (runs unconditionally at boot); dormant via remove_permission() at time of finding (zero production callers).
classification_rationale: Verified via raw two-connection psql sessions against the live yuzu-rbac2703-pg container before and after the fix design.

trigger: A Catch2 REQUIRE fails on the main thread between spawning the CHAOS-1 test's background std::thread and its explicit .join(), or a REQUIRE inside the background lambda itself fails

summary: The CHAOS-1 regression test's std::thread had no join-on-unwind guard; a REQUIRE assertion off the main thread has no exception handler and calls std::terminate() immediately, aborting the whole test binary and losing all remaining tests. classification_rationale: Verified the hazard class; the fix (RAII ThreadJoiner, outcomes moved to atomics, assertions after join) was tested stable across 5 repeat runs.

summary: Fixed in ae03ebfa: RAII ThreadJoiner guard (join, never detach); every thread-produced outcome moved into std::atomic<bool> and asserted only on the main thread after .join(). Verified stable across 5 repeat runs.
